featured_reviews.name: Bijay Bera
featured_reviews.review_text:
1. Shopping Experience
The mall offers a mix of value-for-money national brands and local retailers. It isn’t as "luxury-focused" as malls in South Mumbai, but it covers all essentials.
* Fashion: You’ll find popular anchors like Max Fashion, Pantaloons, and Reliance Trends. It’s excellent for family shopping, particularly for ethnic wear and kids' clothing.
* Daily Needs: Previously home to Big Bazaar, the mall continues to host large format retail for groceries and household goods (now largely under the Reliance umbrella).
* Electronics: Reliance Digital and Digi1 are the main hubs here for appliances and gadgets.
2. Entertainment (The Biggest Draw)
For most locals, Maxus Mall is synonymous with its 6-screen multiplex and gaming zones.
* Maxus Cinemas: Occupying the 3rd floor, this is the most popular cinema in the area. It features various seating tiers, including "Gold Class" and "Director’s Lounge." It is praised for its sound quality (Atmos) and relatively affordable ticket prices compared to city multiplexes.
* Fun Zone & Gaming: There is a large gaming area featuring arcade games, bowling, and VR experiences. It is a major attraction for teenagers and families with young children.
3. Food & Dining
The mall has a massive 100,000 sq. ft. food court area on the 2nd floor, though the variety of "fine dining" is limited compared to fast food.
* Food Court: Offers everything from Dosas (Shreeji Food Court) to North Indian thalis and Chinese. It is generally budget-friendly, with meals for two costing around ₹300–₹600.
* Standalones: McDonald’s (near the entrance) and Not Just Parathas are consistent favorites.
* Note: During weekends, the food court can get extremely loud and crowded, making it difficult to find seating.
4. Infrastructure & Facilities
* Parking: The mall features two-level basement parking. While spacious, it can get chaotic on Saturday and Sunday evenings. Parking fees are typically around ₹60.
* Accessibility: The mall is equipped with elevators and ramps, making it wheelchair accessible.
* Events: It is a central spot for local events, celebrity visits for movie promotions, and festive décor during Diwali and Christmas.

featured_reviews.name: Keval Somaiya
featured_reviews.review_text:
If you’re someone who enjoys ads more than movies, this theatre is absolutely perfect for you.

Showtime? More like “suggested time.” I’ve been here multiple times, and without fail, every single show starts 20–30 minutes late. Honestly, you could walk in 20 minutes after the scheduled time and still comfortably sit through a full ad marathon before the movie even begins.

At this point, missing a scene here is nearly impossible—not because of great service, but because punctuality clearly isn’t part of the experience.

It’s hard to tell whether the staff is just taking it easy or the management has created some magical, impossible turnaround schedule between shows. Either way, the result is the same: frustration.

A 2-hour movie somehow turns into a 3-hour commitment. Impressive… just not in the way you’d want.

Would not recommend if you value your time.

The lift situation wasn’t great either—there’s only one, and it barely fits five people, so getting in and out felt like a waiting game. Inside, there’s just one screen, and honestly, the theatre felt more like a small pod. The viewing experience was okay, but the sound quality could have been way better.

Now, let’s talk about the seats—definitely not the most comfortable. Sitting through a long movie was a bit of a task. On the plus side, the food area was clean, but the prices? Almost as high as PVR, which felt a bit much for the overall experience.

One good thing—they have free underground parking for both bikes and cars, which is a rare win in Mumbai!

Overall, if you’re nearby and just want to catch a movie, it works. But if you’re looking for a top-tier cinema experience, this might not be the best pick.

Cons:

- Less suitable for those looking for a premium experience

Overall, Sona Gold Digital Cinema is a reliable neighbourhood theatre that delivers on value. Great for everyday moviegoers and those who appreciate a more laid-back, no-frills cinema outing.

Rating: 3.8/5

featured_reviews.name: Harikrishna kava
featured_reviews.review_text:
5/5 – Spacious, well-maintained government auditorium with great value

I recently booked this government auditorium for a large event and was really impressed with the overall experience. The hall is huge, with a seating capacity of more than 1,200 people, and it didn’t feel cramped at all even with a full house. There’s plenty of space for stage setup, seating arrangements, and movement around the venue.

What makes this place stand out is the value for money. For a government facility, the booking price is very reasonable compared to private halls of this size. Despite the low cost, the maintenance is excellent. The interiors are clean, the seating is in good condition, and the overall upkeep shows that it’s well taken care of.

The AC works really well and kept the entire hall comfortably cool throughout the event, which is a big deal for large gatherings. The sound system is also top-notch – clear audio, no echo or distortion, and the staff helped us set it up smoothly. Lighting is adequate for both stage performances and presentations.

Location is easy to find and parking was manageable for our guests. The caretaker and support staff were cooperative and responsive whenever we needed help during setup.

For anyone looking for a large, affordable, and reliable venue for conferences, cultural programs, or community events, this auditorium is a solid choice. You get professional-grade facilities without the high private-venue price tag.

Highly recommended.

featured_reviews.name: Dhwani Chavan
featured_reviews.review_text:
We visited Lata Mangeshkar Auditorium in Mira Road to watch a Marathi play. The auditorium is very well maintained and clean. The interiors are beautifully designed and feature memories and tributes to Late Shri Lata Mangeshkar Ji, which gives the place a special touch.
The washrooms were clean, and there are water filters available as well. For food, they have limited options like popcorn, samosa, sandwiches, though the menu may vary depending on the event.
The seating was comfortable, and the management team was cooperative and helpful. The auditorium is fully air-conditioned, but during our visit, the cooling felt a bit low, and it was slightly hot inside.
Outside food items and water bottles are not allowed inside the auditorium. Overall, it is a good auditorium in Mira Road, clean and well maintained, with decent facilities. The only thing I feel is that there should be more plays, concerts, and events happening here because it is a great venue that deserves more activity.

featured_reviews.review_text: Absolutely loved my visit to Bharat Ratna Gaansamragyi Lata Mangeshkar Auditorium! featured_reviews.name: Subhojit Chandra
featured_reviews.review_text:
Visited this auditorium for my daughter's school annual function.

While it is easily accessible due to the location near to the highway, rickshaws to come towards Bhayander are available from the other side only. The highway is dangerous to cross due the speeding vehicles.

Eatables are not allowed inside the auditorium stating that everything is available, but there is just one stall limiting options. The stall was selling cold burgers, cold paneer sandwiches at insane price tag.

There were technical glitches during some performances where audio went mute. Considering the event, it would have been better if the staff had conducted audits prior to the event.The downtime was around 10 minutes but could have been avoided.

Seating arrangements within the auditorium is comfortable but confirm the seat numbers properly. The first row of seats is for VIP guests. Row A is the second row and so on. We were seated in row J but our invitation card showed row K, due to this confusion.
